newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shekel rises against dollar.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shekel rises against dollar.

text.p: The Israeli shekel rose against the dollar on Tuesday in dull trading, dealers said.
"The market was very quiet today and the shekel traded in a tight range. The basket rose mildly and is now around 6.9 percent below the diagonal rate," said Guy Levi of Bank Leumi.
"The recovery of the basket enabled the central bank not to intervene in the market today," he added.

The shekel is allowed to fluctuate in a trading band of seven percent above or below a sloping mid-point designed to devalue the Israeli currency at a rate of six percent a year against the basket of key currencies.

A spokesman for the central bank said on Tuesday that the Bank of Israel is not holding formal talks with the Treasury or working on a package of proposals to ease pressure on the shekel exchange rate.

His remarks come before a scheduled meeting between Bank of Israel Governor Jacob Frenkel and Finance Minister Dan Meridor later today. Sources at the bank and Treasury said they doubted the meeting would produce any concrete proposals.
On Sunday a Treasury official said the bank had spent more than $1 billion during January intervening in the market.

The representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.3160 shekels against 3.3210 on Monday. The basket, composed of the dollar, mark, pound sterling, French franc and yen, was fixed at 3.6299 shekels against 3.6287 on Monday.
On the crosses the shekel traded against the yen at 2.7141 shekels per 100 yen against 2.7206 on Monday and against the mark at 2.0197 shekels against 2.0159 on Monday.
In late afternoon the dollar was trading at 3.3170 shekels.
